steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Nuclear family: two generations (parents and children) living together. Murdock argued the nuclear family is universal and performs four essential functions: sexual, reproductive, economic and educational. Parsons called it the 'isolated nuclear family' - geographically and socially mobile for modern industrial society.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Extended family: three or more generations living together or nearby. Vertical extended: grandparents, parents, children. Horizontal extended: aunts, uncles, cousins. Common in pre-industrial and many non-Western societies; declining in the UK due to geographical mobility.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Reconstituted/step families: formed when adults with children from previous relationships form new partnerships. About 10% of UK families. Challenges: divided loyalties, relationships with absent parent, new family roles and boundaries.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lone-parent families: one parent living with children. About 25% of UK families with children. 90% headed by women. Causes: divorce, separation, choice. Murray (New Right) argues lone parenthood creates welfare dependency; feminists argue it reflects women's increasing independence.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe different types of families and explain how family structures have changed in the UK. | Evaluate the view that the nuclear family is the best family type for society. | Assess the causes and consequences of increasing family diversity.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Murdock: nuclear family is UNIVERSAL (4 functions: sexual, reproductive, economic, educational). Parsons: nuclear family suits INDUSTRIAL society. Nuclear = 2 generations. Extended = 3+ generations. Reconstituted = step-family. Lone-parent = 1 parent. Same-sex = same-gender couple. Family diversity is now the NORM. The nuclear family is no longer the only or even the majority family type.
